Group 42 Blog
Departure: Sunday, June 12, 2022
Arrival in Frankfurt: Monday, June 13, 2022

Please submit text and pictures by 9PM (local time).
June 12 Everybody: Send one picture with a caption or brief description.
June 13 Chloe
June 14 Julian
June 15 Miles
June 16 Brianna
June 17 Taylor
June 18 Mia
June 19 Ethan
June 20 Stella
June 21 Caleb
June 22 Willow
June 23 Lucas
June 24 Chloe
June 25 Julian
June 26 Miles
June 27 Brianna
June 28 Taylor
June 29 Mia
June 30 Ethan
July 1 Stella
July 2 Caleb
July 3 Willow
July 4 Lucas
July 5 Everybody: Send one picture with a caption or brief description.
July 6 Everybody: Send one picture with a caption or brief description.

June 12, 2022

Today we started out journey. The fellas took a picture and then played cards waiting to board. (Caleb)


Crossing the sea? No problem for the mateys! (Lucas)


on the way to metropolis airport!! (Chloe)


Flying over the Atlantic Ocean with the sunset in the background (Stella)


We flew into Dallas and I was very surprised by how flat it was (Ethan)


Leaving for Dallas to start the journey. (Brianna)


Everything is really bigger in Texas (Mia)


leaving the U.S for a month! (Taylor)


Never seen a USB cord vending machine before! (Willow)


Before the 8 hour flight, we had to get our energy out.

June 13th, 2022 (Chloe)

Today we ate at a german cafe and the food was AMAZING. it was something new and had something that most of us have yet to have. we also explored the city of Rothenburg. it was beautiful. we went to both city walls and played frisbee. the weather was good and it was fun to hang out. We took so many pictures and had ate some really good icecream. food here is a lot cheaper than i imaged it would. I think that was something i didn’t expect. the group i was with had decided that we were going to walk along the wall and see across the city. We planned on seeing the tower but the is a plan for tomorrow. --
Chloe


June 14th

On June 14th, we went on a tour of Rothenburg. We went on into a lot of museums and we went into a lot of shops. One tower we went up had a very very tall view. We could see all of the old style houses and their orange roofs. The roofs had shingles in the shape of a beaver tail which was something special to that region. At the end of the day, we went on a tour guided by the night watchmen which was very cool. The church on the left of the picture below had the patron saint of St. James. It needed an extra wing built so they built a portion over a road which was very interesting. Over all, the people didn't have a lot of emotion or reaction to us. We could get away with knowing only basic German. Very touristy city and I think the reat of Germany will be different in the atmosphere, architecture, and civilian encounters. (Julian)

June 15th

Yesterday we celebrated Arthur’s 65th birthday and arrived in Munich. When we got to Munich we played in the park of the youth hostel and played chess on a massive chess board. Then, we took a walk to the U-Bahn and had some time. After the free time we went to dinner and ate Gnocchi and this Potato stuff. After dinner we went down to the game room and played billiard and ping pong until 9:40. Then we went to bed. (Miles)

June 16 Brianna

Today we used the subway for the first time in Germany. We went to the Marienplatz and say a giant mass going on. Then we climbed the city hall tower. You could see over the entire city. Then we went to go grab lunch which was okay. The pasta me and Chloe had earlier this week was better.the we saw a cathedral call Frau Kirchen. It was beautiful.Then we went to BMW Welt and saw some really cool cars and a bike made out of legos. Next we went back to the Hostel to eat dinner. It was pretty good. It was some sort of pasta. The we went to the river and tried to skip rocks. We also had a ping pong tournament. It’s still not finished but I lost to Mia in the first round. (Brianna)

June 17 Taylor


On June 17, we went to the Marienplatz in Munich to hear the music and watch the  glockenspiel. Then after lunch, we took a trip to Dachau which is a concentration camp near where we are staying. It felt unreal to be there and to actually experience where all the horrible things happened to the people who were there.  You could feel there was a somber feeling in the air.  After we went to Dachau we went back to the Marienplatz to shop and roam around in the city center.  It is a very busy place with people, pets, and street performers. Today me and the girls went into shops and got clothes and snacks. Stella and me both got traditional dresses as a souvenir. after shopping we went back to our hostile ate dinner then all the kids played ping pong in the game room! (Taylor)

June 18 Mia


Today we all woke up early because we had to get on the subway to get to a train at the central train station. After that we got to where we needed to be, but then we had to wait for a bus so a bunch of us got some fries from a this small shop nearby. Then the bus finally came and we had to ride another before we could get to the place where will get on a tram to take us up. After all of this everyone ate at the restaurant at the top for lunch and there was also a gift shop. Then we had to do everything again but backwards. Then we ended our day with dinner at the hostel. (Mia)

June 19 Ethan (No Submission yet)

Today we met with our host families in person finally after a long 6 hour bus ride. I watched out the window and got to sort of see the land and compare it to America. I find it very interesting where it is so flat in certain areas, but then just about a mile away is the tallest mountain I’ve ever seen. I’ve met my family on a zoom call before but this was the first time seeing them in person so it was cool and a new experience. The last thing I have to say is how much I miss air conditioning and never realized I took it for granted because I never knew that europeans and or germans do not have it. With the Bergstadt area being the hottest in Germany it feels nice to cool off.

June 20 Stella


Today was our first full day with our exchange students. We went to school with them and had to sit through all of their classes. It was hard to follow along because they were speaking really fast and I didn’t understand anything in the Italian class. Around 11:30, we had a meeting with the principal and gifted him a blanket with a S for Springfield on it. We had asparagus for dinner and we played cards afterwards. It was so funny to try to teach them all of the card games. My exchange partner wanted to learn how to play poker but she didn’t understand it at all. They’re very excited to learn all of the cool games.

June 21 Caleb

Die Mädchen auf der Bergstadter Burg


Today, we started out the day like normal by heading to school, where we had our first period of the day. After that, we were given a list of questions, things to find around Bergstadt in a scavenger hunt sort of game. We spent around 2 hours running around the city and after all points were totaled, the girls took the win over the boys. After that, we went back to school to meet up with our partners for lunch and then have our last class of the day. After school, the fellas (caleb, ethan, julian, miles) all hung out with our partners at ethan’s place. We played soccer and frisbee and had dinner before heading back home for bed. 

June 22 Willow

Today, we went to visit Freiburg in Germany. This involved us leaving Bergstadt on a train, and catching another train to get to Freiburg. We got a tour of the city, which included stopping by a church, given to us by a former teacher at Bergstadt, and we had free time after the tour for a visit to the bakery and for ice cream before we headed back to Bergstadt. And of course, we had to do some shopping. When we got back, I had a computer class with my exchange partner, and we went to her literature class after that. We also decided to go to shops in Bergstadt and go shopping for clothes and books. We wrapped up the day by eating family dinner and watching a movie together.

June 23 Lucas


Today was a nice day, I started the day by being interviewed by 7th graders, all of which had funny questions, such as "do you like Minecraft", "do you like Ronaldo or Messi", and "what's your favorite state". After that I went to school, had an English class that I could follow along with, and met up with Mr Thompson and the rest of Group 42. After that we went on a bus towards Kleinburg, and went to the Rathaus to meet the current Burgermeister and the one before him. It was a pretty cool experience. On our walk to the vineyard we saw 2 grandchildren of the former Burgermeister, and he briefly introduced us. After a small hike up a hill we had lunch atop said hill. The view was amazing. There was beutiful countryside and vineyards as far as the eye could see. Lunch was fun as well. We had lots of bratwurst and they were very delicious. Then after eating we had a brief history lesson about Kleinburg. Shortly after the history lesson we went to a cemetery, and after another game of 'follow the leader' of whomever was in front we realigned ourselves and got ice cream. Then we walked to the soccer field to have a barbecue and celebrate with students and host families, which was moved inside due to heavy winds picking up. After moving inside I helped people get their things inside so they weren't blown away. After closing the blinds, they dented outward. I went to take a look to help when I see Hans and 2 German men whom I didn't know. After helping them fix it we all go back inside and finish eating and enjoy the rest of the time. (Lucas)

June 24 Chloe

Today was an easy day compared to some of the ones that are in the upcoming days. School was different today as the students went through job presentations kind of like the job fairs. it was interesting to listen to what different professions had to say. me and a few other students also spoke to a 5th grade class and let them interview us in english. they asked us all sorts of things and it was hilarious to listen to them freak out over fortnite. All in all today was a good day. i’ll get to see Lukas, Felix, Jonas, and Leon today as well. Although the next few days will be chaotic i enjoy being able just to hang out with svenja. (Chloe)

June 25 Julian

Today was a very busy day. The core four (Julian, Miles, Caleb, and Ethan) and hosts decided to walk up the nearby mountain and have a picnic. The Belchen is the fourth highest peak in the Black Forest and was about a 30 min walk up the windy path. When we go up there, we could see the 4 countries of Germany, France, Austria, and the Swiss Alps peaking above the clouds. It was surreal to see that far and have the prettiest view in all directions. Our picnic consisted of fruits and vegetables along with sandwiches that we brought. After eating, we took the Belchenbahn down which was similar to a closed ski lift. Later, we went to one of our class mate's birthday parties in the evening. (Julian)

June 26 Miles

went to the track to play soccer/ultimate frisbee and played for a few hours. I ended up getting hit in the head with a soccer ball traveling at like 60kmph and my sunglasses are now broken but it was fun. When we took a break from playing we went to an ice cream shop in Bergstadt and it was very good. I then rode a bus back home and it took over an hour because the buses don't drive as much on Sunday. At 9:00 Moritz and I went for a walk and compared Europa Park to Adventureland and talked about the differences between the gymnasium’s school system and Springfield’s. (Miles)

June 27 Brianna


We went to Zurich Switzerland today. After a lot of train rides where me and Mia listened to a lot of music. At about 2:00 we made it to Zurich. First we went to get food as a whole group. Me and Stella got this steak to split. The food there was so good. After we ate our lunch the girls went in one group and we started walking. Our goal was to find Swiss chocolate. We found some at one of the grocery stores. Then we went into a toy store and some people got legos and other games. Next we had to find some ice cream Linda’s recommended 3:00 ice cream. We did and it was some of the best ice cream I have had. When we were done with our ice cream it was time to head back tj the train station and had to go back. All in all Zurich was absolutely beautiful. (Brianna)

June 28 Taylor


On June 28, We went to Europa park. Europa park is a theme park with all the different counties in Europe. I would compare it to Disney in the US because of all the details in the shops, roads, and attractions. Also because the lines we a bit long but that’s to be expected in theme parks like this one. When we first got there me and my group went to get a locker to put the things we don’t need for the day away. no one could figure them out though so we had to ask a employee for help. After that we went on our first ride of the day which was a 4D ride and it took you through Europe. I thought it was a very cute ride.Then we went on a few of the more bigger attractions. For me those were the best because I like rollercoasters. Then it was time for lunch and a couple of us got went to a burger place but i wanted to get asian food so i got noodles with vegetables at a different restaurant. Afterwards it was time for the biggest ride because we got a virtual space in the line for blue fire. We went on the app to get the virtual spot and it worked so we didn’t have to wait in the big line for that one. The last thing we did at the park was get a dessert and we got dutch pancakes. Which were really good, I got the cinnamon and sugar toppings on mine.  It was time to catch the bus back to the train station after that so we ran to the main exit because we didn’t think we would make it on time. In the end we made it and then went back home. (Taylor)

June 29 Mia


Today we went to Strasbourg, France.  Today for me personally i went on a tour throughout a small part of the city then after that we had something called Flammkuchen.  After my friends and I ate lunch we had free time to go around Strasbourg ourselves.  I went to a store where I got a magnet and then we had ice cream.  My flavors were vanilla and and orange sorbet.  After the ice cream some of my friends wanted some sushi so we found a sushi shop so my friends could get some sushi.  After we got the sushi we sat in a alleyway while we ate sushi.  Then it had come to the time where had to go home so we went home and that was my day in Strasbourg, France. (Mia)

June 30 Ethan

Today Caleb, Miles, Julian, and I went to Kleinburg in the morning to introduce the elementary students there to band instruments and were to convince them to join band. I played the tuba, Miles clarinet, and Caleb and Julian trumpet. The clarinets have completely different notes in Germany aswell as the tuba. I had one with 5 rotors to press and I usually only have 3 or 4. It was also in a different key which means the rotors made different notes like the clarinet and I wasn’t able to play it very well. The band director was very funny and definitely convinced a lot of kids to join band since he was a fun guy and made them laugh a lot. It was a cool opportunity for us and we all enjoyed it. When we got back to school we only had sport class left at the end and we played soccer and threw some javelins. None of my friends or I had ever thrown any so it was unique and fun to do. (Ethan)

July 1 Stella

Today we went to school like normal. We had a homeroom today at 9:40 to read the script for the play we watched tonight. We also practiced “Back Home Again in Illinois” so we were prepared to sing it at the celebration tomorrow. We went to the stone quarry, then while we were there we ate some hot dogs and drank some coke. They play started and it was about immagrants coming to America. Just like some of the citizens of Kleinburg did. It was two actors putting it on. One was playing different instruments to set the scene and the other was performing. Then when it was over they had music that we knew playing. We stayed and talked for a while then we went back home.

July 2 Caleb

The highlight of today was the partnership celebration. It was the 37th year of the sister city partnership between Springfield and Kleinburg. Ethan, Julian, Miles, and I all played with the Kleinburg band at the celebration. After the dinner at the beginning, there were lots of speeches by the mayors and the consul generals - the US one living in Frankfort and the German one living in Chicago. My dad (Robert Miller) also had a speech and my sister Sarah translated for him. Near the end of the night, Springfield and Kleinburg exchanged gifts with each other, and the evening came to an end. (Caleb)

July 3 Willow

For today, we started out by walking from the Catholic Church in Kleinburg, and made it to an outdoor area where we celebrated mass together with the people of Kleinburg. It was a wonderful ceremony and a great way to start wrapping up the trip. After this, there was a festival by the Stone Quarry in Kleinburg where there was music, food, and a demonstration by a local stonemason on how stone is used. When I got back to my host family’s house, I worked on gathering my things so I could start packing. After dinner, we then played Uno outside on their patio, and jumped on the trampoline with my host partner’s younger brother. We wrapped up the night by watching Ghostbusters, a movie I had never seen before. (This of course shocked them.) Willow

July 4 Lucas (waiting on picture from Lucas)

Yesterday was pretty interesting because me, Brianna, Mia, and Chloe were asked questions from some sixth graders, but all of them were really shy. Afterwards we began our journey to Gutach. We started with the charter bus, then we picked up some adults who were also in Germany. We then went to the open end museum, which meant there was no roof, took a tour, and then went and got lunch. A lot of people ordered schnitzel for lunch, and lunch went till around 3-4. Following that we had a kinda long bus ride which took us to the building from my first blog in which there was a celebration/mini barbecue. That concludes the whole day. (Lucas)

July 5 Everybody: Send one picture with a caption or brief description.

I will thoroughly miss germany. (Lucas)


The time has really flown by. It seems like just yesterday that I got on the bus at SHS bound for the airport. After an what felt like an incredibly short time, we are now heading home. I will not be coming home empty handed though. I have memories and friendships that I made that will forever stay with me. (Caleb)


today was our last day here so my host family and me went out to eat in Freiburg! (Taylor)


I forgot about this so I’m sending it now (Stella)


Today was our last day. I got home and packed and had some insane sandwiches from the sandwich maker. These are shoes that I wore in Germany they are stinky. (Miles)


Playing Uno with the fam! (I, of course, didn’t win, but I gave it my best effort!) Willow


me and nianas last walk (Chloe)


Family game night with my host family (Mia)


Finn was celebrating a wonderful frisbee catch on our last day in Germany. (Julian)

July 6 Everybody: Send one picture with a caption or brief description.



Ready for the flight (Lucas)


arrived at dallas airport! (Chloe)


On are way back to Dallas, Texas where everything is really bigger in Texas (Mia)


besties sitting by each other again (Stella Out-Of-Data-Smith)


Back in the US and the first stop is McDonald’s. (Brianna)


Finally, after a terribly long day of travel, we made it to the US. (Caleb)


During our layover in the Dallas airport, we collected some delicious Whataburger burgers and shakes. (Julian)



Task:


By cross-referencing the different students' accounts across the entire trip, reconstruct the exact sequence of all events and activities that took place in the town of Kleinburg. Identify any contradictions, omissions, or timeline discrepancies in how different students reported the group's activities. Pay special attention to how locations are referenced across different days.

Based on a cross-referencing of the Group 42 blog posts, the following is a reconstruction of the sequence of events and activities that took place in the town of Kleinburg, along with an analysis of contradictions, omissions, and timeline discrepancies.

### Reconstructed Sequence of Events in Kleinburg

The group visited Kleinburg on four distinct occasions during the trip. The host town for the exchange program was consistently referred to as "Bergstadt," with Kleinburg being a separate location, identified as Springfield's sister city.

**1. Tuesday, June 23, 2022 (Reported by Lucas)**

The group traveled from Bergstadt to Kleinburg for a day of tours and activities.
*   **Morning:** The day began in Bergstadt with Lucas being interviewed by 7th graders.
*   **Travel:** The group took a bus from Bergstadt to Kleinburg.
*   **Rathaus Visit:** They went to the Rathaus (town hall) and met the current Burgermeister (mayor) and a former mayor.
*   **Vineyard Hike:** On a walk to a vineyard, they saw two grandchildren of the former mayor. They hiked up a hill for lunch, enjoying views of the countryside and vineyards.
*   **History Lesson:** After lunch, they received a brief history lesson about Kleinburg.
*   **Cemetery Visit:** The group visited a local cemetery.
*   **Celebration:** They attended a barbecue/celebration at a soccer field with students and host families. Due to high winds, the event was moved indoors. Lucas helped fix some dented blinds.
*   **Evening:** The group finished eating and socializing before presumably returning to Bergstadt.

**2. Thursday, June 30, 2022 (Reported by Ethan)**

A small group visited Kleinburg in the morning to participate in a school activity.
*   **Travel:** Caleb, Miles, Julian, and Ethan traveled from Bergstadt to Kleinburg.
*   **Band Demonstration:** They introduced elementary students to band instruments at a local school.
    *   Ethan played the tuba (noting differences in rotor count and key).
    *   Miles played the clarinet (noting different notes).
    *   Caleb and Julian played the trumpet.
*   **Presentation:** The German band director gave a humorous presentation to encourage students to join band.
*   **Return:** The group returned to Bergstadt in the afternoon for their remaining class (sport class, where they played soccer and threw javelins).

**3. Saturday, July 2, 2022 (Reported by Caleb)**

The group attended a major celebration in Kleinburg marking the sister-city partnership.
*   **Event:** The 37th annual partnership celebration between Springfield and Kleinburg.
*   **Band Performance:** Caleb, Ethan, Julian, and Miles played with the Kleinburg band.
*   **Ceremony:** The event included dinner, followed by speeches from the mayors of both cities and the US/German consul generals. Caleb's father, Robert Miller, gave a speech, which was translated by his sister, Sarah.
*   **Gift Exchange:** The evening concluded with an exchange of gifts between the two cities.

**4. Sunday, July 3, 2022 (Reported by Willow)**

A portion of the group participated in community and cultural events in Kleinburg.
*   **Mass:** The day began at the Catholic Church in Kleinburg, where the group attended a mass celebrated outdoors with the local community.
*   **Festival:** They then attended a festival held by the Stone Quarry in Kleinburg, which featured live music, food, and a demonstration by a local stonemason.
*   **Return:** Willow's post implies she returned to her host family in Bergstadt afterward to pack and spend the evening.

---

### Contradictions, Omissions, and Timeline Discrepancies

**1. Conflicting Activities on July 3, 2022**
*   **Discrepancy:** Willow's post (dated July 3) describes attending mass and a festival in Kleinburg. However, Lucas's post (dated July 4) begins by saying, "Yesterday was pretty interesting..." and then describes a trip to the town of Gutach, including visiting an open-air museum, having schnitzel for lunch, and attending a celebration.
*   **Analysis:** This indicates a significant divergence in group activities on July 3rd. While Willow was in Kleinburg, Lucas (along with Brianna, Mia, and Chloe) was on a day trip to Gutach. The blog posts reflect individual experiences, revealing that the group was not together on that day.

**2. Ambiguous Location of the "Stone Quarry"**
*   **Omission/Discrepancy:** The "stone quarry" is mentioned twice without clear geographic context.
    *   Stella (July 1) mentions going to "the stone quarry" near Bergstadt/Kleinburg to eat hot dogs and watch a play.
    *   Willow (July 3) mentions a "festival by the Stone Quarry in Kleinburg."
*   **Analysis:** It is possible these are the same location, but the posts do not explicitly confirm this. Stella's account does not specify that the quarry was in Kleinburg, only that it was part of the day's activities in the area. Willow's account firmly places the festival quarry within Kleinburg.

**3. Distinction Between Bergstadt and Kleinburg**
*   **Omission:** The blog posts establish that Bergstadt is the primary host town where the students lived with their exchange families and attended school. Kleinburg is a separate town that was visited multiple times. The nature of the relationship between the two towns (e.g., if Kleinburg is a suburb or a nearby village) is never fully explained, which could lead to confusion. The group frequently traveled *to* Kleinburg *from* Bergstadt.

**4. Potential Misattribution of Events**
*   **Analysis:** Lucas's June 23 post mentions a barbecue at a soccer field in Kleinburg. Willow's July 3 post mentions a festival by a stone quarry in Kleinburg. These are clearly two different events, but a reader unfamiliar with the timeline might conflate them. The posts are consistent in describing separate visits.

In summary, the sequence of events in Kleinburg is clear when read chronologically. The primary contradictions arise from the differing experiences of subgroups on the same day (July 3rd) and the occasional ambiguity in location descriptions. The distinction between the host town of Bergstadt and the visited sister city of Kleinburg is a consistent theme throughout the blogs.
